title: Session token integrity (signing, expiry, revocation)
description: Harden session tokens: verify signing/expiry behavior exhaustively, add explicit revocation (logout + callsign-admin wipe), and guarantee tokens never appear in logs.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/session/logout revokes the presenting token (delete row); a second use of the same token returns 401
Tamper tests: any single-character mutation of a valid token (payload or MAC) is rejected
Expiry tests: token with exp in the past rejected; exp within 30 s skew accepted; exp far future accepted
Log-leak test: run a full claim→session→logout cycle with a log sink; assert SESSION_SECRET, raw tokens, and token hashes never appear in captured logs
Concurrent use test: the same token used by two connections — both work until revocation (shared account model, documented)
Unit tests for token codec (sign/verify/tamper/expiry table) green in npm run test

steps.details: POST /api/session/logout: verify token, delete the sessions row. WS: 'logout' message closes the connection with code 1000 after revocation.
Table-driven tests: valid, tampered-payload, tampered-mac, truncated, expired, skew-window, garbage input. All via the same verify() the server uses.

Add a dev-only log sink hook (fastify logger child with a capture stream in tests). Run the full cycle; scan output for the test SESSION_SECRET value, the issued token, and its hash. Fail the test on any match.
Run lint, typecheck, full test suite; commit with conventional message.

technicalNotes: Keep token lifetime at 7 days for v1; remember to rotate SESSION_SECRET guidance in TASK-69 docs.
The log-leak guard should stay in CI as a regression test.
